subject: how to (over)identify unidentified multiple group CFA model?

messages.author: 5dadf4dbf792b603
messages.subject: how to (over)identify unidentified multiple group CFA model?
parts:
Dear all,

I ran into identification problems when I ran the following model:

RIV.model<- '
RIV =~ narq4+narq6+narq9+narq10+narq11+narq12+narq13+narq14+narq17
riv_d =~ narq13+narq14+narq17
riv_a =~ narq4+narq11+narq12'

RIV.unif.f6 <- cfa(RIV.model,Data,orthogonal=TRUE,group="gender",group.equal=c("loadings","intercepts"),
                    group.partial = c("RIV=~narq17","RIV=~narq6","riv_a=~narq12",
                                      "narq6| t1","narq6| t2","narq6| t3","narq6| t4","narq6| t5"),zero.cell.warn=F)

Warning messages:
1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
  lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

2: In lav_model_test(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute scaled test statistic

The problem is I would need the model to be identified because I want to compare the model fit of this model to the fit of the model where the thresholds of item 6 are set equal across gender groups.
Does anybody know how I could change the above model so that it is identified?

Btw, when I run the above model without setting the thresholds unequal, I get a model fit statistic. Also, the model is only unidentified when I set the thresholds unequal for items narq6, narq9, or narq10 but not when I set the thresholds of the other narq items unequal.

I hope somebody can help me out here,
cheers,
Michael

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: how to (over)identify unidentified multiple group CFA model?
parts: the model is only unidentified when I set the thresholds unequal for items narq6, narq9, or narq10 but not when I set the thresholds of the other narq items unequal.

I'm confused.  It sounds like all of the "narq" items are categorical because they have thresholds.  But when you call "cfa" you constrain "intercepts" to be equal across groups -- are you trying to constrain the means (intercepts) of the latent constructs?  Regardless, you are using "group.partial" to free some of the thresholds, but those are not being constrained in the syntax or in the call to "cfa", so you should change your argument to:        group.equal = c("loadings", "thresholds")

I don't know why this would cause this particular error message, but I would be curious to see whether it disappears after getting rid of the seemingly nonsensical "intercepts" constraint in "group.equal" -- I notice the warning only exists when you set the thresholds unequal for items narq6, narq9, or narq10, which are the only items that aren't indicators of two factors, in an otherwise bifactor model...

Terry

messages.author: 5dadf4dbf792b603
messages.subject: Re: how to (over)identify unidentified multiple group CFA model?
parts:
Thanks for your response, Terrence!

The argument group.equal=c("intercepts") does the same as the argument group.equal=c("thresholds") for categorical data. Both equalize the threshold parameters across groups. But, I agree, in order to avoid confusion, it would have been good to use the "thresholds" argument.
Btw, if one wants to equalize the means, then one needs to use the argument group.equal=c("means").

about the identification problem:
Yes, it's a bifactor model and three of the nine items do not have a grouping factor. I also noticed that these three items cause troubles when I set their thresholds unequal across groups. I actually would have expected the opposite, so that there are identification problems with the other 6 items (i.e., the ones that load on both the general and a grouping factor).

Btw, a similar code applied to another 9 item scale ("ADM") also worked fine:
ADM.bf.model<- '
ADM =~ narq3+narq1+narq2+narq5+narq7+narq8+narq15+narq16+narq18
adm_g =~ narq2+narq8+narq1
adm_c =~ narq7+narq16+narq18'

ADM2.f15 <- cfa(ADM.bf.model,Data,orthogonal=TRUE,group="gender",group.equal=c("loadings","intercepts"),
                group.partial = c("ADM=~narq8",
                                  "narq15| t1","narq15| t2","narq15| t3","narq15| t4","narq15| t5"))

no Warning!

the difference between the code for RIV and the code for ADM: for the RIV scale I set the loadings for 3 items free across groups ("narq17","narq6","narq12") whereas for the ADM scale I only set the loading for 1 item free across groups ("narq8"). Btw, these are the items that showed non-uniform DIF in my non-uniform DIF analysis that I did before I tried to test uniform DIF by setting the thresholds uneqal. Therefore, I set their loadings unequal across groups.

best,
Michael
